question: How does the concept of imbalanced classes affect machine learning models, and what strategies can be employed to address this issue?

message.content:
Imbalanced classes occur when one category significantly outweighs others—such as in fraud detection where legitimate transactions far exceed fraudulent ones. This disparity can cause models to become biased toward the majority class, leading to high overall accuracy that masks poor performance for the minority class, such as low recall or F1-score. In some cases, the model may even learn to entirely ignore the minority class.

To address this, several strategies can be employed. Data-level techniques include resampling methods like undersampling the majority class, oversampling the minority class using SMOTE, or using hybrid approaches. At the algorithm level, practitioners can adjust class weights to penalize errors in the minority class more heavily or use specialized algorithms like cost-sensitive learning. Additionally, evaluation metrics should move beyond simple accuracy to include precision-recall curves, F1-score, Matthews Correlation Coefficient (MCC), or AUC-PR. Finally, ensembling methods, such as Balanced Random Forests or boosting techniques, can improve stability and predictive performance on minority classes.
